## Applying for a Master’s degree in France (2027)

Renowned for its rich history in education, vibrant international community and high-quality degrees, **France** is one of the most chosen destinations among students who want to start their Master’s degrees abroad.

With a wide array of English-taught programmes, from Arts to Sciences and Business, the country’s universities have something for everyone. The typical duration for a Master’s program is two years, divided into two separate parts (M1 and M2). Ready to learn more about the ***crème de la crème*** of education?

[**Find a Master in France**](/search?countries=fr&degreelevel=master&sort=recommended)

This guide is regularly fact-checked by our university and admissions experts, most recently in September 2026.

## Step-by-Step Guide

1. ### Find a Master’s programme in France 🔍

   The official Study.eu database lists more than 1,000 Masters in France that are completely taught in English. **[Find yours today!](../../../search?countries=fr&degreelevel=master&sort=recommended)**

   Searching for Masters on Study.eu is the smart first step to any study-abroad plan.
2. ### Levels of Masters in the French system 👩‍🎓

   In the French higher education system, most Master’s programmes are two years long. The first year is referred to as **Master 1** (or **M1**), the second year as **Master 2** (or **M2**).

   Some Masters are only one year long; and some of these might then be a “Master 2”, which would require you to have completed the M1 level of another course.

   There are also **Advanced Masters** or Specialised Masters (**Mastère Spécialisé**). These postgraduate programmes are meant for students that have already completed postgraduate education and want to specialise further. Typically, 5 years of study are required, which you would qualify for with a 4-year Bachelor’s degree and one year of postgraduate studies, or a 3-year Bachelor and a 2-year Master. You might also qualify for admission with 4 years of study and then relevant work experience (typically 3 years or more).
3. ### Know your tuition fees 💸

   **France is known for it’s affordable higher education.** At public institutions, students enjoy the benefit of low tuition fees for Masters programmes:

   * **Students who are citizens of the EU, EEA, Switzerland or Andorra** pay tuition fees of **€243** per year (not quite for free but almost) at universities and usually **€601** at schools of Engineering (but there might be different fees - make sure to ask).
   * **International students from other countries** pay tuition fees of **€3,770** per year for their Masters.

   At private institutions and especially at many of France’s well-renowned business schools the Masters tuition fees will be higher, up to around €25,000 per year.
4. ### Find out how to apply 💡

   The application process for Master’s degrees in France depends on a few main factors: your nationality, your current country of residence, and which type of institution(s) you want to apply to.

   For public universities, it works like this:

   * **You are a national of the EU, EEA, Switzerland, Monaco, or Andorra:** Then you follow the same processes as French students. This means you have to reach out directly to the university to find out how to apply for their Master’s programmes. (If you are planning to study for a Master’s taught in French, you might have to use the national platform [Mon Master](https://www.monmaster.gouv.fr/).)
   * **You are a resident in one of the 72 “Études en France” countries** (see the full list below): Your application will be processed through the [Études en France](https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/etudesenfrance/dyn/public/authentification/login.html) platform. You can use the platform to apply to more than one university. There is an application fee you’ll have to pay; depending on your country of origin, somewhere between €50 and €300.
   * **You are a national of one of those 72 countries, but don’t live in any of them:** In this case you will **not** apply through the Études en France procedure. Instead, contact the university to know which steps you have to take.
   * **You are a national of another country:** Reach out to the university or universities you’re interested in and inquire which process you should follow.

   Private universities and business schools might have their own individual process and separate application platform. Ask them directly to know which steps you should follow.

   Depending on the process, you may have to pay non-refundable application fees. Most universities charge between €75 to €100.

   **The 72** “**Études en France**” **[countries](https://www.campusfrance.org/en/application-etudes-en-france-procedure):** *Angola, Algeria, Argentina, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Benin, Bolivia, Brazil, Burkina Faso, Burma, Burundi, Cambodia, Cameroon, Canada, Central African Republic, Chad, Chile, China, Colombia, Comoros, Democratic Republic of Congo, Djibouti, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Egypt, Ethiopia, Gabon, Georgia, Ghana, Guinea, Haiti, Honk Kong, India, Indonesia, Iran, Israel, Ivory Coast, Japan, Jordan, Kenya, Kuwait, Lebanon, Madagascar, Malaysia, Mali, Mauritania, Mauritius, Mexico, Morocco, Nepal, Nigeria, Peru, Qatar, Republic of Congo, Russia, Rwanda, Saudi Arabia, Senegal, Singapore, South Africa, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, Togo, Tunisia, Turkey, Ukraine, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom, United States, Vietnam.*
5. ### Prepare your application 📝

   To apply for a Master’s degree in France, you typically need to prepare the following documents:

   * Undergraduate degree certificate (for degrees obtained outside France, a translation into French might be required)
   * Proof of English skills (such as IELTS or TOEFL score certificates)
   * A detailed curriculum vitae / résumé
   * A personal statement describing your personal and career goals
   * References or letters of recommendation
   * For non-EU students: a copy of their photo ID/passport, or a copy of the residency permit (*carte de séjour*), or a confirmation of receipt of the residency permit application for the current year
   * Overview of personal work (portfolio, bibliography, thesis, research project, etc.)
   * Questionnaire by the university

   The documents and the required language level may vary depending on the programme. Note that the admissions committee of a school considers not only strong academic performance, but are also interested in students with diverse backgrounds. To improve your chances, **make sure to have extracurricular activities on your CV** such as competitions, internships, leadership in your school or community, volunteering, etc.
6. ### Submit your application before the deadline 📅

   **There is no general Masters application deadline.** Universities in France set their own key dates.

   But some of these can be very early: For starting your studies in autumn, it’s possible that the applications already close in December the previous year. Therefore, do your research early and with time to spare.
7. ### Learn about scholarships in France 🤝

   **Good news:** Except for Paris (which is notoriously expensive), France is generally an affordable country for international students. **Even better news:** There are many scholarships available awarded by both French public and private institutions that cover all kinds of levels and degree subjects.

   Campus France lists many of these grants in its [database](https://www.campusfrance.org/en/bursaries-foreign-students): From scholarships such as “Eiffel Excellence Scholarships” and “Make Our Planet Great Again Scholarships” offered by the French Foreign Ministry; to individual grants funded by each university.

   ***Study.eu Tip:*** French regions and towns allocate scholarships to foreign students enrolled in programmes in their region. Inquire with the admissions staff in order to make sure you are aware of all options available in your university.
8. ### Apply for a student visa for France 🛂

   If you are a **citizen of the EU, EEA, or Switzerland,** you can skip this step since you do not need a visa to study in France.

   **All other international students** have to apply for a long-stay visa valid as a residence permit (visa long séjour valant titre de séjour “étudiant”, abbreviated to [VLS-TS “étudiant”](https://www.campusfrance.org/en/student-long-stay-visa)). This visa allows you to stay in France between four and one year to pursue your studies. Up until three months before it expires, the permit can be extended to a multi-annual residence permit (carte de séjour pluriannuelle).

   International students that are residents of one of the 72 countries included in the “Études en France” procedure will have their VLS-TS application automatically handled once they have submitted their application through the platform. These visas are sent to the French consular authorities of your home country.

   You must validate this visa within 3 months of arriving in France. The process is entirely digital and can be done from your computer.

   **Still unsure if you need a visa and how it should work?** The French government has a [questionnaire](https://france-visas.gouv.fr/en/web/france-visas/visa-wizard) that will help you with all necessary steps.
9. ### Find accommodation 🏠

   As a student, the first step should be researching university-affiliated housing options, such as **student residences.** These dormitories have the advantage of often being the best way to meet other students with whom you can share your questions and experiences.

   If your university doesn’t offer help with accommodation, you can also explore **private rentals** through platforms like *Seloger*, *Crous* or *Le Bon Coin.* Be cautious of potential scams and ensure legal agreements, particularly in Paris.

   Engaging with **local student communities and online forums** can also be a great option in your journey. These platforms provide you with the chance to not only connect with potential roommates but also to build friendships and networks that can enrich your overall study abroad experience from the start.
10. ### Plan your trip 🧳

    **Did you know that Paris is one of the most-visited cities in the world?**

    The French capital has hundreds of direct flights that connect it with most countries on all continents. If you travel from Europe, France’s central location makes it very easy to reach by train or bus.

    Within the country, you’ll find a robust network of high-speed trains that makes it easy to reach other student cities such as Lyon, Toulouse or Bordeaux.

    Bon voyage!

### Typical duration

Masters in France mostly take between 1 year and 2 years to complete.

### Typical tuition fees

At public universities, students from the EU/EEA pay either €243 or €601 per year, and other international students pay €3,770. At private universities and business schools, fees are higher, up to around €25,000 per year.

Written by WTS Visa

Published on July 1, 2026

Every year, thousands of Indian students search for the right IT universities in France and honestly, the confusion is understandable. Between QS rankings, THE rankings, grandes écoles, public universities and dozens of program names that all sound the same, picking the right one for a Computer Science or IT degree can feel like a full-time job on its own. This guide cuts through that noise and gives you a straight, updated list of the top IT universities in France for 2026, along with their rankings, fees, eligibility criteria and admission process, everything you need on one page.

At WTS Study Abroad Consultant, we work with Indian students every day who want to [study in France](https://www.wtsvisa.com/country/study-in-france) but aren't sure where to start. From shortlisting the right university based on your budget and career goals to handling your application, visa documentation and pre-departure prep, our counsellors help you avoid the common mistakes that delay or cause applications to be rejected. Use this guide to build your shortlist, then reach out to us for a personalised evaluation.

## How We Ranked the Best IT Universities in France

This list is built by cross-checking three sources: the QS World University Rankings by subject (Computer Science & Information Systems), the Times Higher Education (THE) rankings and CSRankings, which measures research output specifically in computer science. We also factored in how many English-taught IT programs each university offers, since that directly affects whether Indian students can apply without a French-language requirement. Universities were only included if they had a verifiable Computer Science, Software Engineering, or IT-related department; general-purpose institutions with no dedicated tech faculty were left out.

## Top 10 IT Universities in France

Discover the top 10 IT universities in France known for academic excellence, cutting-edge research, globally recognized degrees and strong career opportunities for international students. 

### 1. Université PSL (Paris Sciences & Lettres)

PSL is the highest-ranked French institution globally and a top choice for students who want to study IT in France at a research-intensive university. It's a collegiate university, meaning it brings together several grandes écoles and research institutes under one umbrella, giving students access to strong AI, data science and applied mathematics programs. Fees are on the higher side compared to standard public universities, but [scholarship](https://www.wtsvisa.com/services/scholarship-assistance) support for high-performing international students is generous.

### 2. Institut Polytechnique de Paris

Formed by a group of top engineering schools, including École Polytechnique, this institute is known for producing graduates with strong placement records in tech and engineering roles. Its Computer Science in France programs are heavily research- and industry-linked, with a focus on AI, cybersecurity and data engineering. Admission is competitive and most master's programs are taught fully in English.

### 3. Sorbonne Université

One of the largest and most recognised public universities in Paris, Sorbonne offers a wide range of IT courses in France, from general computer science to specialised master's tracks in networks, systems and machine learning. Tuition here follows standard public university rates, making it a more budget-friendly option than the grandes écoles without compromising on research quality.

### 4. Université Paris-Saclay

Paris-Saclay consistently ranks among the strongest French universities for engineering, mathematics and computer science combined. It has one of the widest ranges of English-taught master's programs in IT and offers dedicated scholarships for non-EU students, which makes it a popular pick among Indian applicants who want to study IT in France without an extremely high fee burden.

### 5. Grenoble INP

Located in Grenoble, often called France's Silicon Valley due to its dense tech and semiconductor industry, this engineering institute is a strong choice for students interested in embedded systems, IoT and applied computer science. Its close ties with local tech companies mean better internship access during the course.

### 6. Université Grenoble Alpes

A large public university sitting in the same tech ecosystem as Grenoble INP, this university offers computer science and IT programs at public-university fee levels, with solid research output in AI and data science. It's a good balance of affordability and academic strength.

### 7. Aix-Marseille Université

One of the largest public universities in France by student population, Aix-Marseille has a growing computer science department and offers IT programs at some of the lowest fees on this list. English-taught options are more limited here, so check specific program requirements before applying.

### 8. Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1

Based in Lyon, this university has a solid reputation in the sciences, including computer science and applied mathematics. It's a practical option for students who want a well-ranked public university outside the more expensive Paris region.

### 9. Toulouse INP

Toulouse is home to France's aerospace industry and this engineering institute leverages that ecosystem for its IT and computer engineering programs, particularly in embedded systems and automation. Most engineering-track master's programs here are offered in English.

### 10. IMT Atlantique

Part of the Institut Mines-Télécom group, IMT Atlantique specialises specifically in digital technology, telecommunications and IT engineering. If your goal is a highly focused Computer Science degree in France rather than a broad general university experience, this is one of the more specialised options on the list.

## Public Universities vs. Grandes Écoles for IT in France

This is the decision most students get stuck on, so here's the short version. Public universities (like Sorbonne, Paris-Saclay, or Grenoble Alpes) charge government-regulated fees, meaning tuition stays low regardless of your nationality. They're a strong choice if budget is the priority and you're comfortable with a larger, less structured campus environment.

Grandes écoles and engineering institutes (like Institut Polytechnique de Paris, Grenoble INP, or IMT Atlantique) are smaller, more selective and charge higher tuition, but they come with tighter industry connections, smaller class sizes and often better internship-to-job conversion. If your goal is a fast, well-networked entry into the French or European tech job market, a grande école is usually worth the extra cost.

## Admission Requirements for IT Universities in France

Requirements vary slightly between public universities and grandes écoles, but most applications follow this pattern:

* Academic eligibility: A relevant bachelor's degree (Computer Science, IT, Electronics, or Engineering) with a minimum of 60–65% aggregate for most public universities; grandes écoles often expect higher, especially for competitive master's tracks.
* IELTS/TOEFL requirements: English-taught programs typically ask for [IELTS](https://www.wtsvisa.com/ielts-coaching) 6.0–6.5 (or equivalent TOEFL iBT 80–90). Some universities waive this if your previous degree was entirely in English, but it's safer to have the score ready.
* Required documents: Academic transcripts, degree certificates, statement of purpose, letters of recommendation, updated CV/resume, passport copy and proof of English proficiency.
* Application portals: Most public universities process applications through Campus France (mandatory for Indian students), while some grandes écoles and specialised institutes use their own direct portals in addition to Campus France.
* Intake: The main intake for most IT courses in France is September, with applications typically opening in November–December and closing between February and March. A smaller January intake exists at select institutions.

## Best IT Universities in France Based on Your Career Goals

Not every top-ranked university is the right fit for every specialisation. Here's a quick way to match your interests to the right institution:

* Best for Artificial Intelligence: Université PSL, Institut Polytechnique de Paris
* Best for Data Science: Université Paris-Saclay, Sorbonne Université
* Best for Cybersecurity: IMT Atlantique, Institut Polytechnique de Paris
* Best for Software Engineering: Grenoble INP, Toulouse INP

## Career Opportunities After Studying IT in France

France's tech sector has grown significantly and Paris in particular has become one of Europe's fastest-growing startup and tech hubs, alongside established hubs in Lyon, Toulouse and Grenoble. Here's what graduates from IT universities in France can generally expect:

* Average salary: Entry-level IT and software roles in France typically start between €35,000 and €45,000 annually, with roles in AI, data engineering and cybersecurity often on the higher end of that range.
* Top recruiters: Major recruiters for IT graduates include global tech companies with French offices, French tech firms and consulting groups active in digital transformation, along with a strong base of startups in Paris and Grenoble.
* Post-study work visa: France offers international graduates the option to apply for a temporary residence permit (APS – Autorisation Provisoire de Séjour), allowing up to 12 months to search for a job or start a business after graduation, with further extension possible through the Talent Passport route once employed.
* Demand for IT professionals: France continues to report a shortage of skilled tech professionals, particularly in software development, cybersecurity and AI, which keeps demand for qualified graduates, including international ones, consistently high.

With strong industry demand, competitive salaries and post-study work opportunities, France offers excellent career prospects for international students pursuing IT and computer science degrees.

Q1. Which is the best IT university in France?

Université PSL and Institut Polytechnique de Paris currently rank highest globally for computer science and IT-related programs, but the "best" choice depends on your budget, specialisation and whether you prefer a public university or a grande école.

Q2. Can I study IT in France in English?

Yes. Most of the universities listed above, including PSL, Paris-Saclay and IMT Atlantique, offer master's programs fully taught in English, though French language skills can help with internships and daily life.

Q3. Is France good for computer science?

Yes. France has multiple universities ranked in global top 100–200 lists for computer science, a strong and growing tech industry and comparatively lower tuition fees than the UK, US, or Australia for a similar quality of education.

Q4. What are the tuition fees for IT courses in France?

Public university fees for non-EU students typically range from around €2,770 to €3,770 per year for master's programs, while grandes écoles and specialised engineering institutes can range from €4,000 to €20,000 annually depending on the program.

Q5. Is IELTS compulsory for IT universities in France?
